# Data dictionary

**Generated by `python -m docs.build_data_dictionary` from the built warehouse.**
Do not edit by hand -- rerun `make docs` instead.

A hand-maintained dictionary is wrong within a month, because nobody remembers to
update it when a column is added. This one is read straight from the schema, and the
prose comes from the dbt `schema.yml` files, so it cannot disagree with the models.

## main_marts

Dimensional layer. This is what reporting reads. Six conformed dimensions and four fact tables, all defect-free by construction.

### dim_company

Conformed company dimension. Every fact joins to this, which is what makes group-level reporting possible. Carries stores_utc, the flag driving every timezone decision in the project.

`main_marts.dim_company` — **7 rows**

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `company_key` | `INTEGER` | Surrogate and natural key. -1 is the unknown member. |
| `company_name` | `VARCHAR` | Full legal name of the subsidiary, for reporting labels. |
| `company_short_code` | `VARCHAR` | Three-letter code used in source extracts and operational reports. |
| `source_system` | `VARCHAR` | Which ERP this subsidiary runs. Drives the timezone and unit decisions in staging, so it is carried into the mart rather than discarded. |
| `stores_utc` | `INTEGER` | 1 where the source system records timestamps in UTC, 0 where it records local time. The single most consequential flag in the project -- see trap 1. |
| `local_timezone` | `VARCHAR` | IANA timezone this subsidiary reports in, e.g. Europe/Oslo. |
| `is_manufacturing` | `INTEGER` | 1 for the two subsidiaries that run production orders. Only these appear in the labour variance fact. |

### dim_cost_component

Cost breakdown category -- material, labour, overhead, subcontract. Summing a fact across all components without grouping double-counts nothing, but mixing one component's totals with another's is a common reporting error.

`main_marts.dim_cost_component` — **5 rows**

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cost_component_key` | `HUGEINT` | Surrogate key. -1 is the unknown member. |
| `cost_component_code` | `VARCHAR` | Source code, trimmed. |
| `cost_component_name` | `VARCHAR` | Human-readable label. |

### dim_date

Generated date spine. Deliberately excludes the epoch.

`main_marts.dim_date` — **1,826 rows**

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `date_key` | `INTEGER` | Integer key in YYYYMMDD form. Facts carry NULL where no date is known. |
| `calendar_date` | `DATE` | The date itself. |
| `calendar_year` | `BIGINT` | Calendar year. |
| `calendar_quarter` | `BIGINT` | Calendar quarter, 1 to 4. |
| `calendar_month` | `BIGINT` | Calendar month, 1 to 12. |
| `day_of_month` | `BIGINT` | Day of month, 1 to 31. |
| `fiscal_year` | `BIGINT` | Fiscal year on an April start. Differs from calendar_year for January to March, which is a routine source of reconciliation disputes. |
| `fiscal_period` | `BIGINT` | Fiscal period 1 to 12, where period 1 is April. |
| `is_working_day` | `INTEGER` | 0 at weekends. Holidays are NOT excluded -- six countries means six holiday calendars, and inventing one would be worse than being explicit about the gap. |

### dim_item

Part master, conformed across all six subsidiaries. standard_cost is the anchor the ML layer compares each transaction's unit cost against.

`main_marts.dim_item` — **901 rows**

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `item_key` | `HUGEINT` | Surrogate key. -1 is the unknown member. |
| `item_code` | `VARCHAR` | Natural key, trimmed. Arrives fixed-width padded from source -- trap 6. |
| `item_description` | `VARCHAR` | Free-text part description from the item master. |
| `item_family` | `VARCHAR` | Product family grouping, trimmed. Useful for roll-ups. |
| `unit_of_measure` | `VARCHAR` | EA, M or KG. Applies to quantity, not to the labour hours columns. |
| `standard_cost` | `DOUBLE` | Expected cost per unit for this part. The reference point for contextual price anomaly detection -- a unit_cost far from this is suspicious for THIS item even when the absolute value is unremarkable. |

### dim_service_module

The discriminator separating field service, workshop repair, manufacturing and leave. Queries against any fact carrying this key should group by or filter on it, or they risk mixing operationally different businesses into one meaningless number.

`main_marts.dim_service_module` — **5 rows**

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `service_module_key` | `INTEGER` | Surrogate key. -1 is the unknown member. |
| `service_module_code` | `VARCHAR` | Stable code safe to filter on in downstream logic. |
| `description` | `VARCHAR` | Human-readable label for report axes. |

### dim_warehouse

Keyed on company AND warehouse code, because codes are only unique within a subsidiary -- every company has a warehouse called MAIN.

`main_marts.dim_warehouse` — **31 rows**

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `warehouse_key` | `HUGEINT` | Surrogate key over (company, warehouse code). -1 is the unknown member. |
| `company_key` | `INTEGER` | Part of the natural key, not just a reference. A warehouse code alone does not identify a warehouse anywhere in this group. |
| `warehouse_code` | `VARCHAR` | Source code, trimmed. Not unique on its own. |
| `warehouse_description` | `VARCHAR` | Human-readable location name. |
| `is_wip` | `INTEGER` | 1 for work-in-progress locations, which behave differently in costing. |

### fct_inventory_transaction_cost

Inventory cost per transaction. The grain INCLUDES txn_timestamp -- see the model header for why truncating it to a date collapses distinct transactions.

`main_marts.fct_inventory_transaction_cost` — **200,079 rows**

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `company_key` | `INTEGER` | Which subsidiary booked the transaction. |
| `item_key` | `HUGEINT` | Resolved part. -1 where the source code matched no item master row. |
| `warehouse_key` | `HUGEINT` | Resolved warehouse, keyed on company and code together. |
| `cost_component_key` | `HUGEINT` | Cost category this line belongs to. |
| `txn_timestamp` | `TIMESTAMP_NS` | Full timestamp at second precision, converted to the company's reporting timezone. Part of the grain -- truncating it loses rows. |
| `line_seq` | `INTEGER` | Source line sequence. Does NOT restart per day, which is exactly why the grain cannot be built on a truncated date -- trap 3. |
| `txn_date_key` | `INTEGER` | Null where the source carried the epoch, which is correct. |
| `source_item_code` | `VARCHAR` | Original code as received, retained for reconciliation against the source system. Trimmed but not otherwise altered. |
| `source_warehouse_code` | `VARCHAR` | Original warehouse code as received, retained for reconciliation. |
| `source_cost_component_code` | `VARCHAR` | Original cost component code as received, retained for reconciliation. |
| `quantity` | `DOUBLE` | Units moved. A small number of rows carry absurd values -- see is_quantity_reliable rather than filtering on a magic number yourself. |
| `unit_cost` | `DOUBLE` | Cost per unit as recorded. Plausible in isolation even when wrong for the item, which is the basis of trap 10 and the reason the ML layer exists. |
| `transaction_amount` | `DOUBLE` | From source. Never recomputed as quantity * unit_cost. |
| `amount_if_recomputed` | `DOUBLE` | quantity * unit_cost, provided ONLY to make the corrupt-quantity problem visible. Do not report on this column. It is excluded from ML features as label leakage, because it becomes astronomic exactly when quantity is corrupt. |
| `is_quantity_reliable` | `INTEGER` | 0 where quantity exceeds 1e6 and is therefore not usable. Exact, and excluded from ML features for the same leakage reason -- it IS the rule output. |
| `is_wip` | `INTEGER` | 1 where the line hit a work-in-progress location. |
| `is_deleted` | `INTEGER` | Soft-delete flag from source. Filter on this in any reporting query. |
| `is_item_unresolved` | `INTEGER` | 1 where item_key fell back to the unknown member. A count of these is the honest measure of master data quality. |
| `is_warehouse_unresolved` | `INTEGER` | 1 where warehouse_key fell back to the unknown member. |

### fct_labour_hours

Every labour booking across all six subsidiaries and four source systems, with seconds-booked rows converted to hours upstream.

`main_marts.fct_labour_hours` — **150,000 rows**

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `labour_hours_key` | `UBIGINT` | Surrogate key for the booking. |
| `company_key` | `INTEGER` | Which subsidiary booked the time. |
| `service_module_key` | `INTEGER` | Field service, depot repair, manufacturing or leave. Grouping by this is essential -- these are operationally different businesses. |
| `booked_date_key` | `INTEGER` | Null where the source carried the epoch. |
| `employee_code` | `VARCHAR` | Who booked the time. Trimmed. |
| `order_no` | `VARCHAR` | Work order or production order the time was booked against. |
| `operation_seq` | `INTEGER` | Routing step within the order, where the source provides one. |
| `work_centre_code` | `VARCHAR` | Work centre, for manufacturing bookings. |
| `booked_at` | `TIMESTAMP_NS` | Timestamp of the booking in the company's reporting timezone. Legacy sources carry a date only -- check has_time_of_day before using the time component. |
| `work_hours` | `DOUBLE` | Always hours, never seconds. See stg_time_entries_modern. |
| `hourly_rate` | `DOUBLE` | Labour rate applied to this booking. |
| `labour_cost` | `DOUBLE` | work_hours * hourly_rate, computed after unit conversion. |
| `is_productive` | `INTEGER` | 0 for leave and non-chargeable time. Excluding this inflates utilisation. |
| `source_system` | `VARCHAR` | Which extract this booking came from. |
| `source_hours_unit` | `VARCHAR` | HOURS or SECONDS, as stated by the source. The column that makes trap 2 solvable, and the one that is easy to overlook. |
| `work_hours_as_sourced` | `DOUBLE` | The raw value before unit conversion, retained deliberately. Summing this column overstates labour by up to 192x for the affected companies -- which is what makes the trap demonstrable rather than merely described. |
| `was_unit_converted` | `INTEGER` | 1 where a seconds-to-hours conversion was applied to this row. |
| `has_time_of_day` | `INTEGER` | 0 for legacy sources, which carry a date only. A real limitation. |
| `is_deleted` | `INTEGER` | Soft-delete flag from source. |

### fct_labour_hours_variance

Planned versus actual production hours. hours_variance_pct is NULL rather than -100% where nothing was booked -- see the model header.

`main_marts.fct_labour_hours_variance` — **16,380 rows**

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `labour_variance_key` | `UBIGINT` | Surrogate key at the operation grain. |
| `company_key` | `INTEGER` | One of the two manufacturing subsidiaries. |
| `ordered_date_key` | `INTEGER` | Date the production order was raised. |
| `production_order` | `VARCHAR` | Production order number, trimmed. |
| `operation_seq` | `INTEGER` | Routing step. Part of the grain. |
| `work_centre_code` | `VARCHAR` | Work centre the operation is planned at. |
| `operation_status` | `INTEGER` | Source status code for the routing step. |
| `planned_hours` | `DOUBLE` | Planned hours for the operation. |
| `planned_amount` | `DOUBLE` | Planned cost for the operation. |
| `actual_hours` | `DOUBLE` | Booked hours, aggregated to the operation grain BEFORE this join. Aggregating after would fan out planned_hours once per booking. |
| `actual_amount` | `DOUBLE` | Booked cost, aggregated to the operation grain. |
| `booking_count` | `BIGINT` | How many labour bookings rolled into actual_hours. 0 means planned but never worked, which is why the variance percentage must be NULL. |
| `has_actual_booking` | `INTEGER` | 0 where the operation was planned but never booked against. |
| `hours_variance` | `DOUBLE` | actual_hours - planned_hours. Positive means overrun. |
| `amount_variance` | `DOUBLE` | actual_amount - planned_amount. |
| `hours_variance_pct` | `DOUBLE` | NULL where nothing was booked, NOT -100%. A fake -100% reads as "we used no hours" rather than "this has not been worked yet", and drags every average down. |
| `amount_variance_pct` | `DOUBLE` | NULL where nothing was booked, for the same reason. |
| `is_variance_reliable` | `INTEGER` | 0 where the variance should not be reported -- no booking, or planned hours of zero. Filter on this rather than reinventing the logic per query. |

### fct_work_order_lead_time

Order-to-completion lead time per work order. Negative lead times exist in the source and are flagged rather than silently dropped.

`main_marts.fct_work_order_lead_time` — **25,000 rows**

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `work_order_key` | `UBIGINT` | Surrogate key for the work order. |
| `company_key` | `INTEGER` | Which subsidiary raised the order. |
| `service_module_key` | `INTEGER` | Which line of business the order belongs to. |
| `ordered_date_key` | `INTEGER` | Date the order was raised. |
| `completed_date_key` | `INTEGER` | Null for open orders, where the source carries the epoch. |
| `order_no` | `VARCHAR` | Source order number, trimmed. |
| `customer_code` | `VARCHAR` | Customer the order was raised for. |
| `order_status` | `INTEGER` | Source status code. See is_closed for the derived interpretation. |
| `ordered_at` | `TIMESTAMP_NS` | Order timestamp in the company's reporting timezone. |
| `completed_at` | `TIMESTAMP_NS` | Completion timestamp, NULL for open orders. |
| `estimated_value` | `DOUBLE` | Estimated order value from source. |
| `lead_time_days` | `BIGINT` | Raw difference between order and completion. Can be NEGATIVE, because the source genuinely contains completion dates before order dates. Use lead_time_days_clean for any average. |
| `lead_time_days_clean` | `BIGINT` | Null where the raw lead time is negative, so an AVG over this column ignores implausible rows without every consumer having to remember a filter. |
| `is_closed` | `INTEGER` | 1 where the order has reached a completed status. |
| `is_lead_time_plausible` | `INTEGER` | 0 where lead_time_days is negative. Count these to size the problem. |
| `is_deleted` | `INTEGER` | Soft-delete flag from source. |
| `is_open` | `INTEGER` | 1 where the order is still open and therefore has no completion date. |

## ml  (ground truth, not part of the warehouse)

Deliberately **not declared in `sources.yml`**, so no dbt model can reference it even accidentally. The warehouse is built without ever seeing which rows are defective; these labels exist only to score detection afterwards. On a real platform this is where your confirmed incident log lives.

`ml.defect_labels` — **528 rows**

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `company_code` | `BIGINT` |  |
| `item_code` | `VARCHAR` |  |
| `warehouse_code` | `VARCHAR` |  |
| `cost_component_code` | `VARCHAR` |  |
| `line_seq` | `BIGINT` |  |
| `quantity` | `DOUBLE` | part of the join key: passes through staging unchanged, unlike the timestamp |
| `unit_cost` | `DOUBLE` | part of the join key, for the same reason |
| `defect_type` | `VARCHAR` | CORRUPT_QUANTITY, CONTEXTUAL_PRICE, EPOCH_DATE or SOURCE_DUPLICATE |

### Label counts

| Defect type | Rows |
|---|---:|
| `EPOCH_DATE` | 300 |
| `CONTEXTUAL_PRICE` | 162 |
| `CORRUPT_QUANTITY` | 57 |
| `SOURCE_DUPLICATE` | 9 |
